Problem Addressed: Proof-verification flaw in the IAVL hash check allowed forged proofs to release funds
Recommended Solution: Deploy corrected, ICS23-conformant proof verification for all cross-chain packages
Implementation Steps: 1) Freeze non-essential bridge code changes; 2) Implement/merge verifier fix; 3) Independent code review of the diff; 4) Forged-proof regression tests incl. the 2022 attack pattern; 5) Governed hard-fork deployment
Dependencies: Validator coordination for hard fork; independent reviewer availability
Success Criteria: Zero forged proofs accepted in regression and red-team testing; fork live on mainnet
Evidence of Completion: Published release notes and changelog; signed independent review; regression test results
Expected Residual Risk Reduction: Extreme -> High (flaw closed; single-path trust remains until REC-18)

Problem Addressed: Unbounded issuance: nothing limited or interrupted value release from a valid-looking proof
Recommended Solution: Automatic circuit breaker: pause the affected cross-chain channel when unmatched issuance exceeds an approved threshold
Implementation Steps: 1) Define thresholds with governance sign-off; 2) Implement issuance-vs-lock invariant check in the cross-chain module; 3) Wire automatic channel pause; 4) Drill with simulated forged issuance
Dependencies: REC-03 monitoring feed; governance approval of thresholds
Success Criteria: Simulated anomalous issuance above threshold pauses the channel automatically within 5 minutes
Evidence of Completion: Drill report with timestamps; configuration and code references; threshold approval record
Expected Residual Risk Reduction: Extreme -> Moderate for loss magnitude (attack may start; cannot scale)

Problem Addressed: No automated anomaly detection; detection was public/Twitter-driven and a second forgery succeeded 2h17m after the first
Recommended Solution: Continuous invariant monitoring and alerting on bridge issuance, proof anomalies and relayer behaviour, with a paged 24x7 duty officer
Implementation Steps: 1) Instrument issuance/lock reconciliation; 2) Alert rules for proof anomalies (stale block heights, abnormal proof size, burst issuance); 3) On-call rota and paging; 4) Incident record auto-creation
Dependencies: Telemetry access to bridge events; paging tooling
Success Criteria: Test anomalies alert internally within 15 minutes; zero reliance on public channels for first detection in drills
Evidence of Completion: Monitoring configuration export; drill alert logs; on-call roster

Problem Addressed: Relayer admission open to anyone depositing 100 BNB; attacker registered ~90 minutes before exploiting
Recommended Solution: Interim relayer allow-list restricted to vetted candidates, with documented admission criteria and stake/identity requirements
Implementation Steps: 1) Publish admission criteria; 2) Migrate active relayers to allow-list; 3) Disable open registration; 4) Record sunset/re-justification date for the interim control
Success Criteria: 100% of active relayers allow-listed and vetted; open registration disabled
Evidence of Completion: Allow-list configuration; admission records; governance decision record
Expected Residual Risk Reduction: High -> Moderate (interim; centralisation trade-off tracked to REC-13/REC-14)

Problem Addressed: Halt authority informal: validators contacted one by one; escalation depended on individuals
Recommended Solution: Documented emergency authority framework: named incident commander, defined validator quorum, tested 24x7 contact protocol, pre-signed decision templates
Implementation Steps: 1) Draft emergency authority charter; 2) Validator consent and contact registry; 3) Tabletop exercise; 4) Governance ratification
Success Criteria: Tabletop exercise achieves simulated pause decision within 60 minutes using only documented protocol
Evidence of Completion: Charter document; exercise report; ratification record

Problem Addressed: Loss limitation depended on discretionary stablecoin-issuer freezes arranged ad hoc
Recommended Solution: Standing freeze-liaison protocol with major stablecoin issuers and integrators: named contacts, pre-agreed request formats, legal pre-clearance
Implementation Steps: 1) Identify liaison counterparts; 2) Agree request/response formats; 3) Legal review of request templates; 4) Test contact drill
Success Criteria: Drill freeze request acknowledged by each major issuer within 30 minutes
Evidence of Completion: Liaison register; drill log; template pack

Problem Addressed: No public audit report existed for the Token Hub bridge or proof-verification precompile; assurance position could not be evidenced
Recommended Solution: Independent security audit of the proof-verification path and bridge system contracts, with the report published
Implementation Steps: 1) Scope to verifier, CrossChain, TokenHub and relayer contracts; 2) Competitive auditor selection; 3) Audit execution with code-freeze window; 4) Remediation of findings; 5) Publish report and remediation status
Success Criteria: Report published; zero unresolved critical findings at publication or dated remediation plan for each
Evidence of Completion: Published audit report; findings tracker

Problem Addressed: Bug bounty scope ambiguity: the $10M Priority ONE fund targeted projects building on the chain, not the core bridge itself
Recommended Solution: Public bug bounty explicitly covering the core client, bridge and proof verifier, with critical-tier rewards proportionate to potential issuance impact
Implementation Steps: 1) Draft scope naming core components; 2) Set reward tiers; 3) Publish scope on a recognised platform; 4) Triage SLA and disclosure policy
Success Criteria: Core bridge and verifier listed in published scope; first-year triage SLA met
Evidence of Completion: Published bounty scope page; programme metrics

Problem Addressed: Vulnerable code was inherited upstream library code (Cosmos IAVL); dependency risk unmanaged and the flaw affected other projects
Recommended Solution: Dependency governance programme: inventory and pin shared cryptographic/consensus libraries, monitor upstream disclosures, applicability assessment SLA for critical issues
Implementation Steps: 1) Build dependency inventory for consensus-critical code; 2) Pin versions and record provenance; 3) Subscribe to upstream security disclosures; 4) 14-day applicability assessment SLA; 5) Emergency patch path
Success Criteria: 100% of consensus-critical dependencies inventoried; drill upstream critical assessed within 14 days
Evidence of Completion: Dependency inventory; assessment records

Problem Addressed: Massive transfers executed immediately, letting forged value be collateralised on lending markets within minutes ($147.5M borrowed)
Recommended Solution: Timelocks and rate limits on massive cross-chain transfers above an approved value threshold
Implementation Steps: 1) Set threshold and delay parameters; 2) Implement timelock in cross-chain module; 3) Integrator notification; 4) Monitor false-positive impact on legitimate transfers
Success Criteria: 100% of transfers above threshold execute under timelock (KRI 9)
Evidence of Completion: Configuration evidence; KRI report
Expected Residual Risk Reduction: Extreme -> Moderate for contagion speed (with REC-02)

Problem Addressed: Crisis communications concentrated on a single individual (the affiliated exchange's CEO), blurring entity attribution
Recommended Solution: Crisis communications protocol: designated protocol spokesperson roster, pre-approved templates, entity-accurate attribution standard, defined update cadence
Implementation Steps: 1) Name spokesperson roster independent of the affiliated exchange; 2) Draft and approve templates incl. timestamped chronology commitment; 3) Media/social runbook; 4) Simulation exercise
Success Criteria: Simulation produces an accurate, entity-correct holding statement within 60 minutes of L3 declaration
Evidence of Completion: Approved protocol; exercise report

Problem Addressed: Consensus-critical code (including inherited verifier code) could change without a mandated independent review gate
Recommended Solution: Change-management gate for consensus-critical code: mandatory dual review, security sign-off, audit trigger for verifier/consensus changes, emergency-change retrospective
Implementation Steps: 1) Define consensus-critical component register; 2) Implement review gate in release process; 3) Emergency change path with mandatory retrospective; 4) Exception reporting to governance
Success Criteria: Zero ungated consensus-critical deployments in the following two quarters (KRI 7)
Evidence of Completion: Process documentation; release records sample; exception log

Problem Addressed: Validator concentration: 26 active validators and a Nakamoto coefficient of 8 made both attack governance and the halt depend on few parties
Recommended Solution: Validator expansion programme against a published target (active count and Nakamoto coefficient), with transparent progress reporting
Implementation Steps: 1) Publish target and methodology; 2) Candidate validator onboarding pipeline (BEP-131 style); 3) Incentive alignment; 4) Quarterly public progress reporting
Success Criteria: Published target met or on trajectory; coefficient reported quarterly (KRI 8)
Evidence of Completion: Governance publications; validator set data

Problem Addressed: Emergency pause depended on coordinating the full validator set through personal outreach
Recommended Solution: Any-validator emergency channel pause capability (BEP-171 pattern) with misuse safeguards and regular drills
Implementation Steps: 1) Specify pause semantics and abuse safeguards; 2) Implement in cross-chain module; 3) Validator training; 4) Semi-annual pause drills
Success Criteria: Drill: single validator pauses a channel within 15 minutes of a simulated L2 event
Evidence of Completion: Implementation release notes; drill reports

Problem Addressed: Attribution confusion: protocol incident publicly absorbed into the affiliated exchange's reputation; boundaries asserted only during the crisis
Recommended Solution: Entity-separation and incident-attribution standard: pre-documented organisational boundary statement, joint-but-distinct communication protocols with affiliated entities, media briefing pack
Implementation Steps: 1) Publish standing boundary statement; 2) Agree cross-entity comms protocol; 3) Brief analyst/media contacts; 4) Test in crisis simulation
Success Criteria: Simulation coverage attributes the incident to the correct entity in a majority of sampled reporting
Evidence of Completion: Published boundary statement; simulation media analysis

Problem Addressed: Cross-chain contagion: forged assets were instantly usable as collateral across DeFi integrators, multiplying impact channels
Recommended Solution: Cross-chain exposure framework: per-channel value limits, integrator circuit-breaker agreements, contagion stress tests including lending-market collateral scenarios
Implementation Steps: 1) Map integrator exposure; 2) Negotiate circuit-breaker terms; 3) Set channel exposure limits; 4) Run contagion stress test
Success Criteria: Stress test demonstrates contained loss under a repeat of the 2022 scenario within approved appetite
Evidence of Completion: Exposure register; stress test report; integrator agreements

Problem Addressed: Post-incident follow-through incompletely evidenced: promised detailed post-mortem timeline and governance-vote outcomes not located publicly
Recommended Solution: Remediation tracking function with quarterly public attestation: single register of accepted actions, evidence-based status, escalation of overdue items to the risk committee
Implementation Steps: 1) Stand up tracking register; 2) Assign owners and dates to all accepted actions; 3) Quarterly attestation cycle; 4) Public summary publication
Success Criteria: 100% of Phase 1-2 actions attested in-date (KRI 12); zero actions without owner or date
Evidence of Completion: Register extract; attestation publications

Problem Addressed: Single-path trust model: one proof implementation stood between an attacker and unlimited issuance
Recommended Solution: Defence-in-depth verification architecture: second independent verification path (diverse implementation) for high-value releases, with divergence causing automatic pause
Implementation Steps: 1) Architecture design and threat model; 2) Diverse implementation of verifier; 3) Shadow-mode comparison period; 4) Enforce for transfers above threshold
Success Criteria: Divergence between verifiers automatically pauses release in testing; shadow-mode divergence rate within approved tolerance
Evidence of Completion: Architecture document; test results; activation record

Problem Addressed: One-off audit does not sustain assurance over a changing codebase and inherited dependencies
Recommended Solution: Continuous assurance programme: recurring audits on a risk cycle, formal verification of proof-verification code, assurance status published
Implementation Steps: 1) Formal verification of verifier invariants; 2) Annual audit calendar for critical components; 3) Findings lifecycle management; 4) Public assurance page
Success Criteria: Formal verification report published; audit coverage KRI at 100% (KRI 2)
Evidence of Completion: Verification report; audit calendar; assurance page

Problem Addressed: Response capability was person-dependent and unrehearsed; improvement claims require exercise evidence
Recommended Solution: Institutionalised IR exercise programme: semi-annual bridge-compromise tabletop and functional exercises with published performance metrics (MTTD/MTTC)
Implementation Steps: 1) Exercise calendar; 2) Scenario library incl. 2022 pattern; 3) Independent exercise evaluation; 4) Metrics publication and lesson tracking
Success Criteria: Exercise objectives met >= 90% (KRI 11); MTTD/MTTC targets met in functional exercise
Evidence of Completion: Exercise reports; metrics dashboard

Problem Addressed: The single-bridge, dual-chain trust architecture concentrates cross-chain risk in one component
Recommended Solution: Long-term architecture evaluation: assess migration paths that retire or radically reduce the single-bridge trust path (e.g., native or zero-knowledge cross-chain designs), with a decision paper to governance
Implementation Steps: 1) Options analysis with security and migration-risk assessment; 2) Prototype evaluation; 3) Governance decision paper; 4) Migration plan if approved
Success Criteria: Decision paper delivered and decided on the record; no claim of incident causation for pre-existing roadmap items
Evidence of Completion: Decision paper; governance minutes

Problem Addressed: No public evidence of a standing board-level cyber risk reporting line for the protocol; governance visibility was episodic and crisis-driven
Recommended Solution: Standing security governance committee with independent membership, quarterly KRI reporting, and an annual public security governance statement
Implementation Steps: 1) Committee charter and independent membership; 2) Quarterly reporting pack (Section 13 KRIs); 3) Annual public statement; 4) Escalation rights to pause high-risk launches
Success Criteria: Four consecutive quarterly packs produced; annual statement published
Evidence of Completion: Charter; reporting packs; published statement
